unknown.subject: Highway 1.2.0
unknown.evidence: SharedDeps.addSimd links it whenever -Dsimd is on, which is the default; the stripped binary carries no Highway string. Settled by the pinned commit -Dstrip=false build: nm -S finds 12 hwy:: symbols (3,545 bytes) plus 16 Highway-instantiated ghostty::N_{AVX2,SSE2,SSE4,SSSE3} kernels (5,576 bytes), and build.zig.zon pins highway 1.2.0
unknown.settle: Rebuild with -Dstrip=false and rerun nm; the symbol names are stable across the 2% section-size delta between the local and CI builds

unknown.subject: oniguruma, wuffs, simdutf, stb, glslang and SPIRV-Cross byte share
unknown.evidence: the binary is stripped, so no per-component sizes exist. The pinned commit -Dstrip=false build attributes symbol bytes by archive and object membership: SPIRV-Cross 1,735,020; glslang 1,635,275; Dear ImGui 924,031; oniguruma 469,786; wuffs 228,922 and stb 36,445 by prefix; simdutf 222,065; glad GL 55,031; Highway 6,716 (3,545 runtime plus 5,576 in 16 instantiated kernels); sound control socket 4,996; glad EGL 130. The other 21,018,930 bytes in 12,760 symbols are Ghostty own Zig code and runtime plus the per-protocol Wayland glue
unknown.settle: Attribute the symbols of a -Dstrip=false build of the pinned commit; the released binary is stripped and shares no build ID with it, so the shares are evidence about the pinned source, not the shipped bytes

unknown.subject: compiler-rt and Zig-translated C
unknown.evidence: Zig links its own compiler-rt and translate-c output without version strings. The -Dstrip=false build shows 42 Zig-runtime symbols (20,913 bytes), one compiler-rt arithmetic helper (207 bytes), and no translate-c marker string, so no C is incorporated this way
unknown.settle: Zig 0.17.0 source tree for the build, plus an unstripped binary

unknown.subject: Rust crates with build scripts

unknown.subject: 25,121 non-Rust bytes unattributed by play_symbols
unknown.evidence: the residue is the shaderc_util front end, which lives in libshaderc_combined.a and not libshaderc.a; linux-link.args names libshaderc_combined.a. Re-attributing with that archive leaves 17 symbols and 3,257 bytes: crt/main/_init/_fini from musl, rust_eh_personality, the libm forwarders (floor, ceil, round, truncf and float variants) and completed.1/object.0 from Rust self-contained musl libc. The spec named libshaderc.a, so it counted 25,121
unknown.settle: Replace libshaderc.a with libshaderc_combined.a in play_symbols.archives and lower max_unattributed_native_bytes to 4096

components.name: LLVM
components.origin: llvm-static package linked into the Mesa gallium driver

unknown.subject: libgallium LLVM byte share
unknown.evidence: the shipped library is stripped, so the mesa gluon build's -Wl,-Map link map measured it: libgallium-link.map (49,181,662 bytes, sha256 81e64a716aea29803459c87dc6460e8c1efbcde61e3981282a2bb0b3ade90b8a) attributes 44,830,058 bytes in 82,172 live input sections to llvm-static archives, 56% of the 80,492,448-byte linked image and 64% of the 69,526,696-byte shipped file; llvm-toolchain libc++/unwind adds 416,944 bytes in 2,311 live input sections, and all live input sections total 80,655,466 bytes
unknown.settle: Rebuild Mesa through packages/mesa/PKGBUILD.xsh, which rewrites the libgallium link edge with -Wl,-Map=libgallium-link.map and prints the llvm-static, llvm23 and total live input-section bytes to the mesa build log

unknown.subject: Mesa vendored C (xxhash, util, NIR)
unknown.evidence: XXH strings occur, but vendored sources are Mesa own and are not separate dependencies; the shipped libgallium exports 83 symbols through a version script, so no vendored object is a provider

unknown.subject: libvulkan_lvp LLVM byte share
unknown.evidence: the library is stripped, but it exports LLVM dynamically: 26,119 llvm:: symbols carry 14,039,676 of its 15,246,662 dynamic symbol bytes, 92% of that table and 19% of the 72,800,264-byte file
unknown.settle: Re-measure with llvm-nm -D -S --defined-only --demangle on a rebuilt library; a link map would confirm section-level placement

unknown.subject: runtime-loaded libwayland-server.so
unknown.evidence: the string is wayland-backend types::server InitError Display, which compiles in whichever backend is selected. This build selects only the rs backend: the binary imports no dlopen or dlsym, has no libwayland-server.so.0 string, and carries none of the sys backend C entry points (wl_display_create, wl_global_create, wl_display_run), so the string is unreachable. cargo tree -e features shows wayland-backend default plus wayland-sys default only
unknown.settle: A guest run without wayland-libs-server is the remaining behavioural witness; the ELF already proves the path is not linked

unknown.subject: object compiled by clang version 23.1.5
unknown.evidence: .comment names clang 23.1.0-rc2 from the musl crt and libc objects and clang 23.1.5 from crtbeginS.o, which the llvm-toolchain package ships at usr/lib/crtbeginS.o and usr/lib/llvm23/lib/clang/23/lib/linux/crtbeginS.o; rustc 1.99.0 supplies the Rust objects. The object is clang own CRT begin file, not a package source file
unknown.settle: Compare .comment of usr/lib/crtbeginS.o in the llvm-toolchain artifact with the tinyland .comment

unknown.subject: libseat client source language and backends
